text:
maria: Heads up — saw a noisy neighbor in eu-west-2 this morning. Shared pool token cost spiked ~4x and dedicated fallback didn't trigger cleanly :rotating_light:
ashok: Ugh. alloc id? any host/kernel errors?
maria: alloc=pool-shared-eu-09 slot=shared-3 host=172.31.12.45. dmesg had frequent NIC reset lines and `nvlink` saturations. Kernel logs pasted below:
```
[ 12:01:02 ] mlx5_core 0000:82:00.0: NIC reset detected
[ 12:01:03 ] GPU 0: high membandwidth, pcie rx drop
```
rebalancer-bot: Noise detector flagged host 172.31.12.45 for egress-pulse. Started soft-quarantine (5m) and initiated rebalancer at 1761237920.
ashok: short-term mitigation: deprioritize tenant, attach soft-quarantine label and add eBPF policer on NIC. Will open a quick ACL to isolate egress.
leo: If we move tenants into reserved-slice, latency avg goes up ~6ms but cost estimate for warm reserve is ~"$1.1k/day" for eu-west2 at current traffic — rough calc.
sarah: This was driven by a PLG spike from feature flag rollout for customer-X, they pushed a burst of thousands of short-chat requests. Ops already rolled the flag back.
dylan: Can we avoid carveouts by smarter KV cache TTL / batching so bursts don't translate to egress load? Maybe tune cache TTL to 45s for chat tokens. :thinking:
ashok: Agreed on cache tweaks. Also doing NIC shaping now. Quick `tc` to shape 30s microbursts: 
```bash
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 10
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:10 htb rate 800mbit ceil 1g
```
maria: Applied soft-quarantine and bumped reserved weight for shard-reserve-07. Rebalancer moved 12 containers off host; watching GPU mem + egress. Preliminary metrics show egress dropped 82% in 45s. :thumbsup:
rebalancer-bot: Rebalance completed, 12 tasks moved at 1761237920. No failed moves.
leo: Follow-ups: propose adding a 8% capacity hedge for eu-west in Q2 (avoid repeated warmups), and a routing throttle for spikes > X rps that triggers temporary batching window.
sarah: I'll add the cost ask to finance sync and capture the customer incident for postmortem.
dylan: Long term: consider egress-aware routing (tagging tenants with cost-center + burst-profile) so we can prefer dedicated fallbacks only for high-latency-sensitive traffic.
maria: Good plan. For now monitoring at https://monitoring/reports/1761237890 and we'll keep this thread updated if the host flaps again.
